cote-divoire.title: Flag of the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire

colors.note: Hoist-side band representing the savannas of the north and the land's fertility.
Central band symbolising peace and national unity.
Fly-side band evoking the forests of the south and hope for the future.

desc:
- Three equal vertical bands of orange, white and green
- Inspired by the French tricolour, the flag uses African-tuned colours rather than blue and red
- Adopted on 3 December 1959 and kept unchanged after full independence in 1960
trivia:
- Mirror-image of Ireland's tricolour, which has green at the hoist and orange at the fly
- The government has requested since 1986 that the name Côte d'Ivoire not be translated
- Orange also alludes to the country's northern savannas, while green stands for the southern forests
